Harrogate Theatre Panto Tickets Now On-sale Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Masterly
runners_data.note: Returns after a 1077-day absence for Charlie Johnston who does place horses back from breaks, but a single start (third on soft over 9f) gives almost no form foundation and the rust factor is significant at this level.

runners_data.name: Time Thief
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Good going over 10f for Tom Clover and David Egan — the sim-going record of 1W1P on Good is the standout stat, and a prominent tracking position behind Why Not Me is his natural role and the ideal slot in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish runner who prefers to race from off the pace and has placed in both wins and placed efforts over a range of trips, but her best form has come on soft ground and the five-runner field limits the scrimmage that usually brings her into it late.

runners_data.name: Why Not Me
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over on this confirmed front-runner, but she is racing somewhat out of her optimal role at 1m3f given her best form comes over shorter; she should lead comfortably but her stamina over this extended trip is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Feelin' Free
runners_data.note: Ran well when second over 10f on soft last time for Jack Jones, but as a natural prominent type she is effectively displaced in the pace map by Time Thief having a stronger claim to that tracking berth; Connor Beasley will need to adapt her running style in this five-runner field.

races.paceDynamic: Why Not Me is the confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners over 1m3f at Ripon on Good ground, she is likely to slot into a comfortable lead from the outset without serious pressure from the field. Time Thief is the most natural prominent racer in the field and will look to track Why Not Me closely, creating a two-horse front group that sets a measured, sustainable tempo rather than a searching gallop. Peace Belle will be content to settle in rear, while Feelin' Free — a genuine prominent type by nature — is displaced to a midfield slot in the mapping because there are more horses wanting to race near the pace than the small field can accommodate; Time Thief is better positioned to actually secure the prominent berth. The race shape strongly favours a horse that can sit close to an uncontested, honest but not brutal pace and quicken in the home straight — pointing towards prominent or close-tracking profiles as the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Why Not Me controls the tempo and the field strings out early, allowing Time Thief to track and kick.
scenarios.body: Why Not Me dictates a modest fractions on Good ground over the longer trip, and Time Thief, tracking throughout, is poised to pounce turning for home with a clean passage guaranteed in a small field; the proximity to pace is decisive at Ripon's flat, straight-ish finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Why Not Me's gallop proves too strong for trackers and the pace is more relentless than anticipated.
scenarios.body: Why Not Me, uncontested and finding her rhythm over a trip that suits a stamina-biased front-runner, simply grinds on as the field fails to quicken past her; the lack of pressure paradoxically allows her to conserve energy through the middle stages and tough it out late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to set things up for a late run from rear.
scenarios.body: Peace Belle, versatile over this type of trip, is the only genuine hold-up runner and would need the front pair to have burned each other out; in a five-runner field with a controlled pace, getting a decisive late run from off the pace is difficult and she would need a clear track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Masterly, returning from a near three-year absence, has been quietly prepared to peak on this comeback.
scenarios.body: Masterly's Unknown competitive fitness after 1077 days away is a major caveat, but Charlie Johnston can place horses off long breaks and this trip may suit a horse with a stamina profile; the race shape would need to fall perfectly with a generous pace to bring a rusty horse into it late.

watchPoints.text: Time Thief's proximity to Why Not Me's uncontested lead is the pivotal tactical factor — watch whether David Egan allows a gap to form or sits tight, as close tracking on Good ground at Ripon over 1m3f is the profile this race shape rewards most.

Why Not Me's stamina for 1m3f is unproven — if she ties up in the final two furlongs having set the pace, the race is blown open for those tracking, so monitor how freely she travels through the middle stages.

Feelin' Free's ability to adapt from a prominent to an effective midfield role will determine her relevance; Connor Beasley will need to make a quick decision at the start about whether to push forward or settle, and either option carries compromise.

Masterly's 1077-day layoff makes her a watch from a welfare and market-move perspective — any significant gamble from a wide price would warrant attention given Johnston's capability with returning horses, but treat the form lines as essentially blank.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Ripon Champion Two Yrs Old Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Napa
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's front-runner returns after a 95-day break stepping up to 6f for the first time; won over 5f Good last time and the going is fine, but the OR=91 mark and distance query make her a pace-pressure contributor rather than a likely winner — Jason Hart will send her forward regardless.
runners_data.comment: Napa landed the spoils two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and the prevailing ground, while his rating of 96 marks him out as a leading player from stall three; the main concern is that eighth last time out and a 95-day absence since.

runners_data.name: Pure Mint
runners_data.note: Crisford's OR=120 powerhouse is the standout on ratings and won her sole 6f start on Good ground, which is a direct course-and-distance match; Harry Davies rides with confidence and the step up in class from a debut win rarely fazes this yard's best juveniles — the central question is whether four rivals hassle her into a pace duel she doesn't need to have.
runners_data.comment: Pure Mint won last time out and brings strong recent form into this, having run over today's trip before; rated 102 and top of the field, he looks the one to beat off 131 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Bear Lee
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's hold-up juvenile has run four times and recorded his only win over 5f Good, so stepping to 6f against Listed company is a significant ask; Billy Garritty will hold him up off the strong pace and hope the closers' scenario unfolds, but the OR=77 baseline makes him reliant on a collapse in the front group to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has finished fourth and fifth in her two most recent outings, so consistency is the query; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 126 lb from stall eight, and returns fit on a 12-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Clash Of Hearts
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's front-runner has a headgear flag and has made the frame in five of his runs including a 6f Good win, giving him course-relevant form; Sheehy will drive him forward to dispute the early lead, and while his consistency is admirable, he's the one most likely to be outgunned by Pure Mint's superior class if they end up racing side by side.
runners_data.comment: Clash Of Hearts won three starts back and was placed before that, giving him a lively recent profile, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the concern is that his last two runs have seen him slip to fifth and eighth.

runners_data.name: Harry Knows
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's prominent racer has an exceptional record in similar conditions (5 of 6 runs producing a win or placing on Good ground), and McDonald is one of the shrewdest pace-readers in the north; positioned just off the lead he can exploit the front-runner battle without sacrificing energy, and his OR=87 may flatter his market position less than it appears given his consistency.
runners_data.comment: Harry Knows arrives here in solid nick, a winner two starts back and placed either side of that effort, bringing strong recent consistency over today's trip and ground; the slight concern is that his last run was a third, suggesting he may need to reproduce peak form.

runners_data.name: Not My Type
runners_data.note: William Haggas has this unbeaten filly stepping from 5f to 6f in Listed company, which is a double ask, and Marquand will need to decide whether to let her stride forward or restrain her behind the pace brigade; both wins came over 5f Good so the going is fine, but whether her speed translates to a longer trip against stronger rivals is the key uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of eight on our figures despite two consecutive wins in her last two starts, Not My Type arrives in fair nick 18 days since her last run and has run over today's trip, but a speed rating of 67 makes her hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Rogue Jewel
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's dual 6f winner on Good ground brings a perfect 2-from-2 record at the trip, and Tudhope's tactical awareness will allow him to sit prominently without overextending early; OR=86 is the bottom of the weights and the horse is unbeaten, meaning any upside in his rating feeds directly into this scenario — his profile is almost identical to Harry Knows structurally.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Jewel arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but she ranks seventh of eight on our figures and that gulf is hard to overlook despite her obvious recent momentum.

runners_data.name: Silent Beauty
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's prominent type has a 73-day absence to overcome, and her Ripon form showed a 23rd-place finish on Good (6f) before winning on Soft — the going switch back to Good is a mild concern and the long layoff adds risk; David Egan will look to place her prominently, but she enters as the most uncertain quantity in the field on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Silent Beauty returns after 73 days off having won two starts back, though she was unplaced last time out and our rating of 87 leaves her with something to prove against this field.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Mint, Napa, Clash Of Hearts, and Not My Type all profile as front-runners, meaning four horses will be pulling toward the same piece of real estate at the break, virtually guaranteeing a strong, contested early gallop over Ripon's straight 6f. Pure Mint is the highest-rated of the pace brigade at OR=120 and has the class to boss the lead if she gets first run, but Clash Of Hearts and Napa will be pressing hard from stalls to the two-furlong pole, creating genuine pressure rather than a false or manufactured tempo. Not My Type, unbeaten in two but stepping up from 5f, may find the pace too hot too soon if she tries to dictate against this calibre. This contested, strong-pace scenario over a flat 6f on Good ground systematically favours horses who can track the speed from a prominent or midfield position and sustain their effort through the final furlong — horses like Harry Knows and Rogue Jewel, who can race handy without burning reserves early, are structurally best-positioned by this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Mint Dominates From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Mint breaks cleanly and uses her class superiority to control the pace without being seriously harassed.
scenarios.body: Pure Mint's OR=120 dwarfs the field and her single run — a winning 6f debut on Good — maps perfectly to this course and distance; if she settles into a rhythm rather than scrapping for the lead she can dictate and kick clear when Crisford's horses typically find their best form second time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner battle between Napa, Clash Of Hearts and Not My Type burns each other out, allowing the prominent stalkers to swoop.
scenarios.body: Harry Knows has a formidable record tracking pace on Good ground (1W4P in similar conditions) and McDonald will position him to exploit any front-runner fallout; Rogue Jewel, a dual 6f winner for Bethell and Tudhope, profiles identically and both will be cruising just off a scorching early clip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner War, Closer Sneaks
scenarios.trigger: If all four pace horses fight furiously to the turn and the pace becomes genuinely suicidal, leaving a trail of beaten leaders.
scenarios.body: Bear Lee is the only genuine hold-up runner in the field and Billy Garritty will be riding him cold off a 12-day turnaround; the Easterbys' 2yo has shown a win on 5f Good and could pick up the pieces if the field strings out ahead of him in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Not My Type Surprises On Step Up
scenarios.trigger: If Not My Type — unbeaten but untested over 6f — translates her brilliant 5f form to this trip with Haggas's preparation lending her extra class.
scenarios.body: Haggas's unbeaten two-year-olds often carry a sizeable performance reserve on their handicap mark, and Marquand will be able to settle her once she accepts the step to 6f; if she switches off early and travels, her raw ability could be decisive, but the pace dynamic remains a genuine threat to this scenario materialising.

watchPoints.text: Pure Mint vs Clash Of Hearts — if these two lock horns for the lead in the first two furlongs the pace will be genuinely testing and front-runner chances across the board diminish rapidly.

Not My Type's trip stamina — Haggas has her stepping up 1f for the first time in Listed grade; if she doesn't settle early for Marquand she could run out of room in the final furlong and underperform her unbeaten record.

Silent Beauty's 73-day layoff — Philippart De Foy runs two horses here but Silent Beauty has had the longer break and her only Good-ground 6f run produced a distant finish at Ripon itself; fitness must be monitored in the preliminaries.

Bear Lee's viability as a closer hinges entirely on the pace war scenario materialising — if Pure Mint controls the tempo sensibly, the 6f trip on a flat track offers no terrain for a hold-up horse to generate the momentum he needs from OR=77.

Rogue Jewel and Harry Knows share almost identical style, going, and trip profiles — whichever of the two gets the better early position behind the pace could split their market support and the one better placed at the two-furlong marker is likely to be the more dangerous finisher.

races.name: Ripon Rowels Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: English Oak
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with strong recent course-relevant form (2nd over 8f on Good, two wins at 7f on Good), well-suited by today's Good ground; Harry Vigors' 5lb claim is a neutral factor but the trainer's 2/15 14-day record is modest — the key asset is a clean finishing kick if the prominent group ties itself in knots.
runners_data.comment: English Oak ran second two starts back and arrives here fresh enough on 31 days' rest, with experience of today's distance and going working in his favour; the unplaced effort last time is the one mild reservation, but two wins in his last six starts underline the ability at the weight.

runners_data.name: Thunder Roar
runners_data.note: Returned from 87 days off and carries a headgear notation (p); the sim-going record of just 2/15 on Good ground is the starkest red flag here, and back-to-back 15th and 16th finishes in recent starts make it very hard to argue this hold-up type can improve enough on stable form to feature.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and unplaced in three of them, Thunder Roar nevertheless carries a rating of 101 from stall seven over a trip and going he has experience of, making him a leading threat on paper — the chief concern is whether 87 days off the track has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: Tagged with a tendency to fade in the finish which is a significant liability in a race where the prominent group will already be under pressure from 2f out; O'Meara's 3/39 14-day trainer strike rate is low, and ten from fifteen sim-going runs without a win signals this horse runs consistently but rarely finds that extra gear at the death over 8f on Good.
runners_data.comment: Rated 94 and carrying 133 lb from stall six, Mirsky has experience of today's trip and conditions and returns fit on an 11-day turnaround, but his recent string of ninths makes it hard to see where the improvement comes from.

runners_data.name: Mr Professor
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride for Kevin Philippart De Foy whose 3/14 14-day stat is respectable; the horse's best Good-ground 8f performance is a second at Kempton (Standard) and it has placed twice from three runs on anything approaching Good — a hold-up style that could benefit from the prominent group's congestion, though the absent win from Good-turf conditions is a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Mr Professor returns on a quick turnaround of just 12 days, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and his runner-up finish last time out makes him a live danger, with our rating of 93 underscoring his claims; the concern is he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Racingbreaks Ryder
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's presence is the single biggest jockey upgrade in this field and gives this prominent runner the best chance of any horse to cleanly navigate the four-way position battle in the early stages; two recent wins over 7-8f on Standard give confidence in the stamina and tactical speed, though the one sim-going run (1/15) is a small sample — form rather than going is the draw here.
runners_data.comment: Racingbreaks Ryder has back-to-back wins two and three starts back, though he was well held in eighth last time out and carries 128 lb from stall nine; he has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid grounding, but that recent reversal is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Spoken Truth
runners_data.note: O'Meara's second runner, and a confirmed hold-up horse whose natural style is at the rear of the field — mapped here to midfield only because the race shape has more closers than the visual allows; the 0.93 style-fit discount reflects the likelihood it won't get the clean, late-developing race it needs, and its best form has come over 9-10f rather than today's mile.
runners_data.comment: Spoken Truth has run over today's distance and going before and shaped with promise last time out when finishing third, though he remains winless in his last six starts despite a string of placed efforts, making him a consistent but frustrating type at 127 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Milteye
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, proven at 8f and able to set his own fractions from an apprentice-ridden, 125lb berth — a genuinely interesting in-running angle; the soft-ground wins are worth noting (1/8f/SOF twice) and Good may be slightly quicker than ideal, but the uncontested lead gives Harriet Bethell's gelding a clear structural advantage whatever the final result.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last two starts, Milteye's recent form makes him hard to fancy despite a win three starts back, and he ranks seventh of nine on our figures; experience over today's trip and going at least means conditions hold no fresh fears.

runners_data.name: Firefall
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old returns after 68 days off with a form string of 1-9-8-2 that includes a win over 10f on Standard and a runner-up over 8f on Good — the trip shortens for today and the Good turf surface is different from its Standard all-weather run, but the prominent style and yard's 4/27 14-day record make it a legitimate contender to secure second position behind Milteye early.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Firefall showed he can mix smart form with moderate efforts — a winner four starts back, and a second last time out after disappointing runs in between, suggesting he may be returning to his best after 68 days off.

runners_data.name: Majestic Dane
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's 9/44 14-day trainer record is the best stat in the race and this three-year-old has shown class with two runs and a win over 7f on Standard — but 193 days off and a step up in both trip and competition to a 9-runner 1m Good-turf handicap is a significant ask; the prominent style suits the likely shape, but the fitness question after over six months absent must be weighted heavily.
runners_data.comment: Majestic Dane returns after a lengthy 193-day absence and, rated 65 against a field of eight rivals, it is hard to make a case for him despite a second last time out and experience over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Milteye is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only a 5lb apprentice claim on board from Ethan Tindall, should be allowed to coast to the front and set a genuine but unhurried Good-ground gallop over this flat Ripon mile. Behind him, Mirsky, Racingbreaks Ryder, Firefall, and Majestic Dane all want prominent positions, creating a four-way scramble for the places directly behind Milteye in the first two furlongs — traffic and bumping between these horses from the jump is a real concern approaching the 2-3f marker. The field holds more prominent types than can cleanly be accommodated, meaning at least one of Racingbreaks Ryder, Firefall, or Majestic Dane will be pushed wider or deeper than ideal; Racingbreaks Ryder (Oisin Murphy aboard) and Majestic Dane (K.R. Burke's excellent 14-day record of 9/44) are best-placed by rider and handler quality to actually secure that prominent berth. A controlled, single-paced lead from Milteye on Good ground favours hold-up horses with a strong late turn of foot who can track a steady early fractions and finish powerfully, with the genuine hold-up runners — English Oak and Mr Professor — best-positioned to exploit any prominent-group congestion and fatigue in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Milteye Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Milteye dictates a moderate pace unchallenged and the prominent group traffic burns each other off, freeing a clear late run for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Milteye sets fractions comfortable enough to keep himself in contention but the four-wide prominent battle leaves those horses leggy in the final 2f, opening a clear rail or wide berth for hold-up types to finish strongly; Good ground with no rain suits powerful finishers over this flat Ripon mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble settles quickly within the first furlong and one horse breaks cleanly to sit second, tracking Milteye into a well-paced contest before outkicking rivals late.
scenarios.body: The early jostling resolves fast, allowing one prominent runner to ghost into a perfect stalking position 2 lengths off Milteye and use Good-ground positional advantages to hold off late challengers; this shape rewards horses with natural stamina at the mile trip and tactical speed to quicken from a prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion results in no genuine challenger pressing Milteye and the field dawdles, leaving him with an uncontested lead and enough reserves to sprint clear from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Milteye, a proven front-runner with four wins and four places from eight runs and a solid record at 8f on softer ground, has the profile to exploit a truly uncontested lead; his apprentice rider's claim may mask market anxiety but the horse's tactical positional speed makes him dangerous if given a completely free passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Chaos Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group collectively sets a stronger-than-expected early pace through their positioning battle and the race becomes a rough-and-tumble test of stamina rather than tactical speed.
scenarios.body: A fractious, contested early pace on a flat track with nine runners can occasionally produce a rough-ground winner from a horse that avoids the melee and stays wide; Spoken Truth, though mapped here to midfield rather than its true hold-up position and carrying a 0.93 style-fit discount, has course-relevant form at 9-10f and could get an uninterrupted run if chaos opens gaps.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic: Mirsky, Racingbreaks Ryder, Firefall, and Majestic Dane all targeting the same early positions — watch for bumping and checking between the 7f and 5f markers as four horses contest two or three spots directly behind Milteye.

Milteye's pace: if Ethan Tindall (apprentice, 5lb claim) settles Milteye too conservatively and the pace collapses, a tactical sprint develops over the final 2f that transforms this from a closers' race into a positional battle — monitor the early splits.

Majestic Dane's fitness: 193 days off the track for K.R. Burke's three-year-old is an obvious flag — watch how sharply it begins and whether it travels with fluency in the first half of the race, as a stiff absence can mask underlying condition even from a top yard.

Spoken Truth's position: Daniel Tudhope will try to place a hold-up horse in a race with limited natural cover at the rear — watch whether it gets a clear run between the 3f and 1f markers or gets boxed in behind the tiring prominent group.

Thunder Roar's headgear (p) fitted today after a lengthy 87-day break — watch for a positive market move or notable market drift as a signal of stable confidence given the poor recent form figures in anything approaching Good ground.

races.name: Book Online At Ripon-races.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist for Gemma Tutty with strong recent 5f good-ground form (three wins, six places in similar conditions); Connor Beasley knows this horse well and will likely track wide in the final furlong to find daylight, which is the key tactical requirement here.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and third three starts back, Mark's Choice arrives fit on 16 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the risk is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f good-ground performer returning just five days after her last run; Tim Easterby's yard is in solid form (4/71 14-day), and Fentiman will need a clean early break to actually hold prominent position in what is a crowded early berth.
runners_data.comment: Canaria Queen has been consistently placed, finishing second in three of her last six starts including last time out, and has run over today's distance and going before — her consistency makes her a leading danger, though she remains yet to score and converting that placed form is the key question.

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old has been placed twice in five recent 5f good-ground starts and carries the headgear flag; the reality is that four horses want the same early ground, and Sullivan will need immediate sharp work to avoid getting crowded out in the opening furlong.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Betweenthesticks faces a stiff task, with a trainer running at just 4% in the past fortnight the most damaging context; a third three starts back offers slim encouragement, and he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's eight-year-old has winning form over 5f good going and boasts two wins from his last five; Jason Hart is the key asset — an experienced handler of traffic — though the horse's inconsistency (wins interspersed with 9th-place finishes) is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Ran fifth last time out off a break of just five days, but a winner two starts back and rated 80 by us — the highest-ranked of the nine runners — Our Absent Friends has experience over today's trip and going, and that prior form makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's hold-up specialist has three wins and six places from eleven good-ground 5f runs and is ridden by Oisin Murphy, the standout jockey booking in the field; his natural back-of-field style means traffic is less of an issue, and Murphy's ability to find a run makes this a genuine player in Scenario B.
runners_data.comment: Rock Of England landed a win three starts back and arrives here fit on a 17-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going, our rating of 77 marking him a leading danger; the risk is that he has finished fourth in each of his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Thornaby Pearl
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, uncontested for lead, with four wins and eight places from nine good-ground 5f outings; Oliver Carmichael takes a 7lb claim which effectively sharpens the value, and the absence of early pressure is the single biggest race-shape advantage available today.
runners_data.comment: Thornaby Pearl won last time out and has form over today's trip and going, but he carries a hefty 137 lb from stall 8 and our rating of 71 places him fifth of nine, suggesting he faces a stiff task against the top-rated rivals here.

runners_data.name: Glory Fighter
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old Paul Midgley hold-up runner whose recent form has dipped (three consecutive finishes of 5th, 6th, 6th) but who has one soft-ground run in the last five that may flatter the recent figures; David Nolan will need everything to go right positionally to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Glory Fighter has experience over today's trip and going, and his win five starts back gives him a recent marker, but three consecutive finishes out of the frame make him hard to fancy wholeheartedly; 131 lb from stall 2 adds another layer of consideration.

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Four-year-old from the busy Easterby yard (4/71 14-day) returning quickly after nine days; has placed at 5f on good ground but overall record in similar conditions (2 wins, 3 places from 11 runs) suggests a horse that needs things to drop right rather than one who makes his own luck.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below most of her rivals on these figures and ranked eighth of nine, Marajito is hard to fancy despite a quick turnaround of nine days; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a second two starts back offers some encouragement, but a seventh last time out does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Happier
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley's six-year-old carries strong recent form (two wins in last four) and rates well on a low OR of 61, but by nature wants to race prominently — in this field that position is overcrowded, so Harry Vigors (5lb claim) will find the horse racing further back than ideal, which tempers confidence in its ability to reproduce that winning form today.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Happier faces a stiff ask despite being lightly exposed, though she arrives in decent nick after a winning run two starts back and a runner-up finish last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Thornaby Pearl is the confirmed lone front-runner here and, with no genuine speed rival to pressure her through the early stages of this 5f Ripon sprint, she can control tempo from the gates and set a pace entirely on her own terms. Behind her, a congested group of prominent-racing types — Canaria Queen, Betweenthesticks, Our Absent Friends, and Marajito — will jostle for the two or three positions immediately behind the leader, creating significant traffic danger between the 2f and 3f markers as they shuffle and bump for ground. The hold-up horses Mark's Choice, Rock Of England, and Glory Fighter will be forced to navigate whatever gaps remain from the back of that pack, while Happier, a natural prominent racer that cannot find its preferred slot in this crowded field, is mapped to midfield but will not race with the fluency its style demands. The redistribution of Happier confirms this field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Canaria Queen and Our Absent Friends look likeliest to actually secure their natural position given their recent rhythm and draw. This race shape tilts in favour of the confirmed front-runner Thornaby Pearl, who faces no pressure to burn early, and secondarily rewards hold-up horses with the ability to find a clear run in the final furlong on a track that historically suits closers who travel wide.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pearl Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Thornaby Pearl jumps cleanly, establishes a comfortable lead without being pressed, and sets a sustainable gallop that drains the prominent pack chasing her.
scenarios.body: Thornaby Pearl dictates from the front in her own time, and the congestion among the chasers means the hold-up horses lose momentum negotiating traffic rather than building a telling challenge; the leader reaches the final furlong with reserves intact.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic battle mid-race is so severe it burns pace faster than expected, leaving the field ragged entering the final furlong and opening a clear passage on the outside.
scenarios.body: Rock Of England and Mark's Choice, both holding good recent 5f form on good ground, travel wide to avoid the congestion and pick off a tiring leader in the last 75 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If one of the chasing prominent runners breaks cleanly, avoids the mid-race traffic scramble, and locks onto Thornaby Pearl's quarters from the outset.
scenarios.body: Our Absent Friends, a multiple 5f winner on this going and lightly weighted relative to class, or Canaria Queen with strong recent placing form at the trip, tracks the leader throughout and gets first run in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scenario Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runner congestion causes crowding or interference two furlongs out, disrupting Thornaby Pearl's rhythm and scrambling the finish.
scenarios.body: A clean-travelling outsider — Glory Fighter or Happier navigating outside the carnage — could benefit from a chaotic finale, though Happier's displaced style means it is unlikely to be ideally placed to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Watch Thornaby Pearl's early strides — if she is squeezed or slow away at the gates, the sole pace advantage that underpins Scenario A evaporates and the race becomes wide open.

The four prominent runners (Canaria Queen, Betweenthesticks, Our Absent Friends, Marajito) will collide for the same two positions between the 4f and 3f marks — any interference or crowding here could cause interference to multiple runners and benefit those tracking widest.

Rock Of England is the key beneficiary of a fast pace — watch whether Murphy positions him on the outer from the off to avoid the prominent scrum, as a wide run from the back is his most likely winning route.

Happier's starting position in the stalls could partly determine how displaced it ends up — a low or unfavourable draw compounds the natural problem of being a prominent type unable to find that position in a crowded field.

Our Absent Friends carries a notably inconsistent recent record (1st, 9th, 1st, 9th pattern) — if this is an "off" day for the horse, Jason Hart may find himself with no response when Thornaby Pearl quickens clear.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Classified Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer with strong course and distance form at this 1m2f trip, recording a win and three placings in 15 similar-going starts; James Sullivan knows this horse well for Ruth Carr and the prominent-running style is perfectly aligned to the single-leader race shape here.
runners_data.comment: Copper And Five shaped with real promise when runner-up last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, with his rating of 55 giving him a squeak against this field; yet to score in his last six starts, and a trainer firing at just 4% is the concern.

runners_data.name: Inspiring Speeches
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with every chance to control tempo from the front; Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) keeps costs down and Sara Ender's stable has been quiet (0/3 over 14 days), but the tactical position is the key asset — uncontested leaders at Ripon on Good ground are hard to catch.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Inspiring Speeches does offer some encouragement with a third three starts back, though consecutive fourths since suggest he finds a way to be competitive without quite getting there; carrying 135 lb from stall 3, experience over today's trip and going at least removes unknowns.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for Tim Easterby who has been placing regularly without winning; David Allan rides and the nine-year-old's two recent seconds suggest consistency, though the single-leader scenario may not produce enough pace for him to finish through on the bridle.
runners_data.comment: Placed second three starts back and again four starts back, Little Ted arrives on a sharp 16-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, and our rating marks him as the one to beat here — though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rogers Dream
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on this authentic hold-up performer for Gihan Arnolda, and while Murphy's class is a clear plus, the horse is a true rearward type placed in midfield on the map because the field has more hold-up horses than positions — the lack of strong pace is a real concern for his style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Rogers Dream nonetheless brings consistent placed form into this, including a third last time out and two fourths before that, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in her favour; 135 lb from stall two is the challenge.

runners_data.name: Top Gun Tina
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie partners this six-year-old for David Thompson after a 58-day absence; she is an honest hold-up type whose best form is on Standard surfaces rather than Good turf, and having been pushed into a midfield slot by redistribution, the race shape does not naturally suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and rated just 44 officially, Top Gun Tina faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 50 offers a shade of encouragement; 58 days between runs is a query returning from stall four carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Volenti
runners_data.note: Sam England's seven-year-old has three placings in seven good-ground runs and consistently performs in the 3rd-4th bracket; Oisin Orr rides and the horse is best placed as a genuine tracking hold-up type who could capitalise if the field compresses, making him one of the more credible threats from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Volenti has finished third on two occasions in his last six starts — last time out and three starts back — showing consistent placed form despite being yet to score, and he has run over today's trip and going; the 43-day absence is the main query.

runners_data.name: Due To Shine
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes this Brian Ellison three-year-old — a 3lb allowance carrier — who showed promise placing at Southwell and Nottingham but has form on softer surfaces; as a true hold-up runner that the map has moved to midfield, the controlled tempo expected here is not what she needs to produce her best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Due To Shine faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 31 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but that may be the limit of the encouragement.

runners_data.name: Princess Coco
runners_data.note: The Andrew Elliott/Simon Whitaker three-year-old has a ⚠ fade flag and returns from 77 days off with a questionable recent form string (including two zeros); she is a genuine rearward runner slotted to midfield by redistribution, and both the fitness question and the finishing pattern make her an outsider here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Princess Coco faces a stiff task here; 77 days off the track does little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and is at least familiar with conditions.

runners_data.name: Trucial Pearl
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's mount for the Michael & David Easterby yard won six starts ago over 8f on Good ground and ran just six days ago — the quick return bears watching for freshness; her form trajectory is improving and she is one of the younger hold-up types with a realistic chance of finishing through if the race pace sets up late.
runners_data.comment: Trucial Pearl was a winner three starts back and brings strong fitness having run just six days ago, with experience of today's going working in her favour; the risk is that she has finished fourth in each of her last two starts.

runners_data.name: Twin And Tonic
runners_data.note: Cian Horgan (5lb) partners this Roger Fell three-year-old on just his third career start; the ⚠ fade flag and 39-day absence are concerns, and as a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position, the inexperience combined with a race shape that demands tactical patience makes this a low-probability runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Twin And Tonic faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and the 39-day break may have freshened her up.

races.paceDynamic: Inspiring Speeches is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should slot into an uncontested position from the off, controlling tempo over this 1m2f trip on Good ground at Ripon. The pace is likely to be honest rather than frantic — a single leader setting a sustainable rhythm on a flat, galloping track suits a settled, even-tempo race shape. This configuration classically rewards horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can track the leader without expending unnecessary energy and then pounce in the straight. The dominant profile here is the prominent racer or close-tracking type; Copper And Five is ideally suited to sit just behind Inspiring Speeches, while true hold-up horses face an unfavourable shape if the tempo is controlled. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Rogers Dream, Top Gun Tina, Due To Shine, Princess Coco, and Twin And Tonic are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed on the map, with Volenti and Little Ted most likely to secure the natural tracking positions behind the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Inspiring Speeches Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches leads uncontested at a sustainable gallop and the race develops into a steadily-run test of finishing quality.
scenarios.body: Inspiring Speeches sets a comfortable tempo, the field strings out in orderly fashion, and horses racing prominently or just off the pace conserve energy to challenge in the final two furlongs; hold-up horses from far back find insufficient time to close on a track that does not play to extreme late finishers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Copper And Five and Inspiring Speeches share the early pace and produce a genuine front-two gallop that racks up ground on the field.
scenarios.body: The early duelling between the two prominent types produces a stronger pace than anticipated, which paradoxically suits horses with tactical speed who can stay in touch at close range; the race becomes a test of which of these two types sustains best into the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough to compress the field and create a sprint finish where redistributed hold-up horses get a clear run from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A dawdling early gallop concertinas the field and gives horses like Volenti and Trucial Pearl — who hold genuine claims on form — a realistic chance to quicken off the slow pace in the final furlong; true hold-up horses Rogers Dream and Due To Shine remain disadvantaged by their natural style even in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast and the principals tire badly in the final furlong, gifting a late run to a horse from the rear.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires both Inspiring Speeches setting a strong pace and the prominent horses burning out — a low-probability combination given the single-leader dynamic and Good ground; Princess Coco and Twin And Tonic carry fading-in-finish flags that make them unlikely beneficiaries even here.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Inspiring Speeches is allowed a truly uncontested lead — if anything pushes for the front early, the entire pace dynamic shifts and hold-up horses gain ground.
Trucial Pearl ran just six days ago; monitor in-running for any signs of fatigue in the final furlong given the quick turnaround, as this will determine whether her improving profile holds up.

Oisin Murphy's booking on Rogers Dream is significant class above typical for this grade — if the hold-up shape develops in Murphy's favour, Rogers Dream could outrun his redistribution disadvantage despite it being against his natural race style.

Volenti has finished 3rd or 4th in seven consecutive runs — watch whether Oisin Orr attempts to ride him more aggressively to secure a tracking position rather than his habitual rearward berth, which would change his win probability materially.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Rogers Dream, Top Gun Tina, Due To Shine, Princess Coco, Twin And Tonic) all competing for midfield slots could create traffic issues on the turn into the straight — watch for crowding as horses make their moves from 3f out.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Classified Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Back From Dubai
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who showed ability with a course win at a similar trip and is the lone pace-setter here; Roy Bowring sends him back after 18 days and he is perfectly suited to controlling from the front on good ground, though his trainer's recent 0/2 record tempers confidence slightly.
runners_data.comment: Back From Dubai shaped well when third last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, with our rating of 55 suggesting he holds strong claims from stall seven; the worry is that his form has been patchy in recent starts, with only one win to his name.

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Phoenix
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old has the best trainer-14-day strike rate in the field (4/71) and has placed twice on good ground in her last five; a natural hold-up operator who will settle at the rear and rely on the pace being strong enough to reel in Back From Dubai, which is far from guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Evelyn's Phoenix nevertheless appeals on his rating and returns here on a quick turnaround of 15 days, carrying 135 lb from stall one, with experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour.

runners_data.name: Golden Samba
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this lightly-framed four-year-old who is a thorough stayer on form (16f-17f trips in recent history) dropped sharply in trip here; holds up naturally but pushed forward on the map, and 63 days off the track adds a fitness query on top of the trip-suitability concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Golden Samba faces a stiff task here; her sole encouragement is a third three starts back, though she returns after 63 days off and has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides a horse with genuine course-and-distance form (third over 10f on good ground) and a solid placed record at the trip; naturally suited to sitting close enough to the pace to challenge late, and his sim-going record of 1W/5P suggests he consistently runs his race on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Quirke On Parole shaped with some promise when third last time out, and she has run over today's distance and going before, yet she remains winless in her last six starts and a mark of 48 leaves her mid-division on ratings heading into this.

runners_data.name: Tiberio Force
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old fitted with a hood and coming off a run just 16 days ago; his last five runs are a string of mid-pack finishes on good and standard ground at this trip, and while he is a deep closer by inclination, the slow pace likely on offer will make it hard to pick up horses from off the bridle.
runners_data.comment: Tiberio Force has run over today's trip and going, and at 16 days freshened up he arrives in reasonable nick, but a winless run of five starts showing a consistent drift toward the back makes improvement essential if he is to feature from stall five carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Crumpet
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose form figures read 8-8-9-11-10 in his last five outings — the worst sequence in the field by some distance — and who reverts to a p-headgear after 37 days off; his natural hold-up style is entirely unsuited to a slowly-run race and improvement seems unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Wheres The Crumpet faces a stiff task from stall two carrying 135 lb, and her recent finishes offer little encouragement; however, she has run over today's distance and going before, and a rating of 46 leaves a small margin for improvement.

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Three-year-old apprentice-ridden (Rhys Elliott, 5lb claim) who has never won in eight starts but has finished fourth and fifth on good ground; naturally a hold-up type, his youth makes him the most adaptable runner in this bunch, and the claim could offset some of the positional disadvantage if he secures a midfield pitch.
runners_data.comment: Balance Of Trade shaped with encouragement when fourth three starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, while our rating of 53 puts him ahead of his official mark; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must reverse a run of below-par efforts.

runners_data.name: Captain Bruce
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Andrew Crook (no runners in 14 days) who is tagged as fading in finishes and has not placed in five career starts; a natural deep closer whose 63-day absence and consistent fade pattern make it difficult to identify a favourable scenario for him regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Captain Bruce has been winless in his last five starts, with a string of eighth and ninth-place finishes offering little encouragement, and our figures rank him ninth of ten here. The 63-day absence is a concern, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Retro Rocket
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old for Martin Keighley (1/3 in 14 days) with only four runs on the clock, all resulting in mid-to-rear finishes; fitted with a p-headgear and ridden by 5lb claimer Harry Vigors, his inexperience is a clear unknown, though the trip here — longer than anything he has tried — adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with finishes no better than sixth in that sequence, Retro Rocket is hard to fancy on these figures, though 25 days between runs at least suggests he arrives fresh and draw four is a neutral enough pitch.

runners_data.name: Ten Sixty Six
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old handled by Daniel Tudhope is the form pick of the hold-up horses with a 9/10 good-ground sim record and three placed efforts from his last six; having never won in nine starts he has been consistently competitive, and tracking the pace at a trip he handles well gives him a genuine each-way profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Ten Sixty Six nonetheless brings fitness from a run 18 days ago, experience on today's going, and a speed rating that nudges ahead of her official mark — the risk is that recent form offers no clear upward trajectory.

races.paceDynamic: Back From Dubai is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 1m2f contest and, with no genuine rival willing to press for the lead on good ground at Ripon, should be able to control the tempo from the front without being seriously challenged. The pace is therefore likely to be measured and sustainable rather than searching, giving Back From Dubai a genuine opportunity to dictate throughout and preserve energy for the straight. Behind him, the bulk of the field — including Ten Sixty Six, Quirke On Parole, Evelyn's Phoenix and others — are natural hold-up horses who will be forced to hunt the leader from varying distances back. This race shape strongly favours the lone pace-setter and any horse capable of tracking closely enough to challenge in the final two furlongs, rather than pure closers who need a strong gallop to deliver their best; true late-runners will find the pace too conservative to be fully set up for them. Several runners including Balance Of Trade, Captain Bruce, Tiberio Force, Wheres The Crumpet, Retro Rocket and Golden Samba are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains far more deep closers than there are rear positions available; of these, Balance Of Trade and Tiberio Force are the most likely to actually push forward and claim a midfield berth in running.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dubai Controls Soft Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai is allowed to stride clear and set an uncontested, measured pace throughout the 1m2f trip.
scenarios.body: Back From Dubai dictates every fraction on good ground, keeping the tempo low enough to preserve his stamina reserves, and the hold-up horses behind him are simply unable to generate the momentum required to reel him in off a slow early pace. Horses who have tracked closely — Ten Sixty Six or Quirke On Parole — are best placed to challenge, but the front-runner's head of steam makes him very hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If a close-tracking hold-up horse such as Ten Sixty Six or Quirke On Parole is smartly positioned just off the pace and has enough left to collar Back From Dubai inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The leader keeps them honest but the pace is just honest enough for a well-placed rival who has sat two or three lengths off the front to produce a late challenge on the good ground that suits quick finishers. Ten Sixty Six's consistent good-ground profile and Quirke On Parole's proven form at this trip both make them the likeliest beneficiaries if the front-runner begins to tire in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up Sharply
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly in the back straight, either through a rival pressing Back From Dubai or a strongly-run middle section that string the field out.
scenarios.body: A faster-run race tests stamina more thoroughly and marginally increases the chance of a genuine hold-up horse staying on through beaten rivals, though most of the closers here have modest recent form and face significant style-fit penalties having been pushed into midfield roles. Evelyn's Phoenix, the most consistent hold-up performer in the field on good ground, would be the primary beneficiary, with Golden Samba a secondary candidate if the redistribution from the rear proves advantageous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai is taken on for the lead early or races keenly and stops abruptly in the straight, scrambling the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish with no horse having raced in an ideal position would hand a marginal edge to any horse who switches off early and avoids traffic, but the low overall quality of hold-up runners here — most carrying significant style-fit discounts — means the outcome is largely unpredictable. Balance Of Trade, the youngest runner and least set in its ways, could exploit the disorder better than established hold-up types.

watchPoints.text: Back From Dubai's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single most important factor — if he is left alone in front at a steady pace, the entire field is essentially chasing a potentially unassailable advantage by the time the straight arrives.

Ten Sixty Six and Quirke On Parole are the two most credible dangers to the front-runner, but both must secure a prominent early position to have any chance; watch the first two furlongs to see whether either jockey (Tudhope, Hart) commits to tracking Back From Dubai closely.

Evelyn's Phoenix, Tiberio Force and the other redistributed hold-up runners will need a much stronger gallop than this race shape is likely to produce — if they are buried in rear positions going into the final turn, the slow pace will leave them with too much ground to make up.

Golden Samba's drop from marathon trips (16f-17f) down to 1m2f is significant; watch whether Joanna Mason rides her forward to compensate for the shorter trip or attempts her usual hold-up tactics, as the approach will affect whether she gets competitive at all.

Balance Of Trade, ridden by a 5lb claimer, is the youngest in the field and the most unpredictable positionally — if Rhys Elliott elects to push forward early rather than settling at the back, he could insert himself between the pace-setter and the hold-up pack and complicate the race for everyone behind.

races.name: Aja Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer with a solid Good-ground record and 8 starts at similar going, finishing second at 12f on Good last time; Daniel Perrin's 7lb claim is valuable and the 1m3f trip suits a horse who stays all day, though it has not won since recording sim-going form figures of 1W3P.|
runners_data.comment: Spirit Catcher arrives here 21 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating has him top-rated by four points — yet he is winless in his last six starts, with only a pair of seconds to show among recent efforts, so he needs to rediscover that placed form at stall four off 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Jam Lass
runners_data.note: Carries a 133-day absence as its biggest concern; showed a win and a placed effort on Good going in its sim-going record and trainer Niven is 1/2 in the last 14 days, suggesting the yard is in form, but the layoff over this trip with an inexperienced amateur in the saddle is a material risk.|
runners_data.comment: Jam Lass won four starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving her every chance to recapture that form from stall five carrying 156 lb; the chief concern is returning from a 133-day absence.

runners_data.name: It's Only Fun
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has placed three times at similar going without winning; the 4yo has Good-ground experience at 12f and the trainer has had no winners from three runners in the last 14 days, but its hold-up style is genuine and it arrives fresh enough at 25 days since last run.|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last six starts — a second four runs back and a winner five runs back — but three subsequent efforts have yielded only mid-to-rear finishes; he has experience over today's trip and going, and at 155 lb from stall 6 returns fit enough after 25 days off to make the argument, though his rating of 63 suggests he faces a stiff task against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Woodleigh
runners_data.note: Roger Fell sends this 5yo out just nine days after its last run — freshness is not a concern — and it carries genuine Good-ground form with two wins and three placed efforts in 15 sim-going starts; however, it is a natural hold-up type pressed into a midfield map position by the density of closers in this field, which will require it to race closer to the pace than it prefers.|
runners_data.comment: Woodleigh won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform, though he carries 153 lb from stall 9 and his form has been patchy in between, with three fifths in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: The Easterby yard is 4/71 in 14 days, an active and productive spell, and this 7yo wears a hood and has genuine Good-ground experience at 10f; it is a natural prominent-racer and should travel comfortably behind the two front-runners, though its last run was a flat zero in a 10-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Kitsune Power arrives here just 16 days after his last outing, bringing experience of today's distance and going, and a win four starts back gives him a proven winning thread; the main concern is that he was unplaced on his latest start.

runners_data.name: Cougar
runners_data.note: A true hold-up specialist whose 12f Good-ground history shows no placed efforts in the last five runs and 0 wins from 15 sim-going starts; absent 47 days and, being naturally suited to racing off the pace, it will find its preferred ground at the rear but faces a field shape that may not deliver the late cover it needs to produce a telling finish.|
runners_data.comment: Cougar has won in recent starts but four subsequent efforts have yielded two fifths, a seventh and an unplaced run, making him hard to fancy ranked ninth of ten on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and stall three is at least a neutral draw.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: The race's most likely pacesetter; a hat-trick of Good-ground places and a recent win at 10f gives it the best pace-related profile in the field, and Charli Parker's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable; the contested early gallop with On The Bubble is the key variable — if Star Start controls that duel it becomes a serious contender to last home.|
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner two starts back, Star Start arrives here on a quick turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour, though a 4% trainer strike rate of late and 151 lb on his back are notable drags on his chances.

runners_data.name: Three Yorkshiremen
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have come on Soft or Standard, giving it just a 1/15 sim-going record and significant Going concern; a natural prominent-racer who may follow the leaders, but the drop from Stamina tracks and unfamiliar Good ground makes this a highly speculative proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Three Yorkshiremen has little recent form to recommend him; he does have experience over today's trip and going, and a 41-day break may have freshened him up, but the weight of 150 lb makes the task harder still.

runners_data.name: Glitter Code
runners_data.note: The Bethell yard is 4/27 in 14 days and this 4yo has placed five times at similar going without winning; a natural hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map due to the surplus of closers in this field, meaning it may not get the wide, late run it needs — the style-fit discount is real and its chance depends heavily on the race developing into a proper test.|
runners_data.comment: Glitter Code arrives here 26 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 63 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 56 implies — a second four starts back hints at that latent quality; the risk is a winless recent run of five.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Arrived just four days after its last run and is the co-pace-maker alongside Star Start; five Good-ground starts including two places at 12f gives it some credentials but it has never won on Good ground and is likely to find the early duel costly in the final furlong; the fresh return is a watch point for Emma Brown's 5lb claim doing a job if it settles.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last on our figures, On The Bubble faces a stiff ask here; a second four starts back offers a crumb of comfort, but a seventh last time out and a quick four-day turnaround make her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Star Start and On The Bubble are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over Ripon's 1m3f trip, creating a genuinely contested early gallop on Good ground rather than a lone leader dictating an easy tempo. With two horses fighting for the front, the pace is likely to be honest throughout, compressing gaps and putting a premium on stamina and the ability to travel smoothly in behind before delivering a sustained late effort. Three Yorkshiremen and Kitsune Power will look to press from just off the pace as natural prominent-racers, adding further pressure to the mid-sections and reducing the chance of the race slowing to a crawl. This shape — a competitive, even gallop over a genuinely stamina-testing trip — strongly favours hold-up horses with proven Good-ground form who can deliver a clean, progressive finish, particularly Spirit Catcher, Jam Lass, and It's Only Fun. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can naturally accommodate at the rear; Woodleigh, Cougar, and Glitter Code are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map, and with Star Start and On The Bubble certain to lead, it is Star Start who is most likely to secure the rail position and On The Bubble the outside lead, leaving the redistributed trio to race wider or further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Star Start and On The Bubble force a genuine gallop and the race is run at honest fractions throughout, enabling hold-up types to pounce in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace drains the leaders and prominent horses, opening the race for those held up and produced late; Good-ground stamina becomes the defining quality over the final quarter-mile at Ripon.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Star Start Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Star Start establishes a comfortable lead over On The Bubble and is allowed to control tempo, conserving enough to kick clear turning for home.
scenarios.body: A front-runner who dictates on a flat, Good track and is not run off its feet early can build an unassailable advantage by the two-furlong marker; Star Start's strong Good-ground record and recent placed form support this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the leaders tire badly early, promoting the prominent-running Kitsune Power or Three Yorkshiremen into contention through straightforward attrition.
scenarios.body: A moderating gallop can suit horses who travel prominently and save ground on the bend; Kitsune Power's recent course-form at 10f and the ability to sit just off the pace without burning energy makes this plausible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Overwhelmed by Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up types — Woodleigh, Cougar, Glitter Code — are forced further back than usual and cannot make up ground from deep over this trip.
scenarios.body: Racing genuinely out of role in a contested-pace scenario, these horses face a compounded disadvantage of starting position and trip; the scenario resolves into a race where neither true closer nor natural frontrunner wins, and a progressive hold-up type with better positional flexibility edges it.

watchPoints.text: Star Start and On The Bubble will dispute the lead from the outset — watch whether Star Start gains a clean break at the off and controls the contest; if On The Bubble pushes hard early, both may empty before the final two furlongs and hand the race to hold-up types.

Jam Lass returns from 133 days off and has the profile to be spot-on first time back for Peter Niven (1/2 T14), but an extended absence over 1m3f on an undulating track with an amateur jockey means it must be monitored early for signs of rustiness or lack of fitness.

Woodleigh, Cougar, and Glitter Code are all natural hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to field congestion — watch where they actually settle at the start; if all three drop to the rear regardless, the rear of the field could be extremely congested and they will need to find room simultaneously in the straight.

Three Yorkshiremen has run exclusively on Soft or Standard going in its last five starts and its sim-going record stands at just 1/15 — monitor its early action and whether it travels with any fluency on today's Good surface, as a poor traveller here would confirm the Going concern.

Kitsune Power wears a hood and the Easterby yard is in a productive 14-day spell; watch whether Miss Collier positions it immediately behind the two leaders, as a prominent horse that gets a clean run could benefit disproportionately if the pace war between Star Start and On The Bubble is severe enough to open gaps in the straight.
